31 The diagram shows two metal plates P and Q. There is a potential difference of 700 V between
the plates. Plate Q is earthed.
–700 V
plate P
R
5.0 mm
plate Q
0 V
What is the magnitude and direction of the electric field at point R?
A
1.4 × 102
N C–1 from P towards Q
B
1.4 × 102
N C–1 from Q towards P
C
1.4 × 105
N C–1 from P towards Q
D
1.4 × 105
N C–1 from Q towards P

hints: Notice plate P is at $-700\text{ V}$ and plate Q is at $0\text{ V}$, so the potential difference magnitude is $700\text{ V}$ across separation $5.0\text{ mm}$.
Recall for parallel plates the uniform field magnitude is $E = V/d$, so you must convert $5.0\text{ mm}$ to $0.0050\text{ m}$ before dividing.
Recall electric field points from high potential to low potential, so compare $0\text{ V}$ on Q with $-700\text{ V}$ on P to decide between towards Q or towards P.
walkthrough: Identify the uniform field region: point R is between parallel plates P and Q with separation $d = 5.0\text{ mm} = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$ and potential difference magnitude $V = 700\text{ V}$.
State the governing relation for a uniform electric field: $E = V/d$, with $E$ in $\text{N C}^{-1}$ when $V$ is in volts and $d$ is in metres.
Substitute values with units: $E = 700 / (5.0 \times 10^{-3}) = 140000\text{ N C}^{-1} = 1.4 \times 10^5\text{ N C}^{-1}$.
Determine direction: electric field points from high potential toward low potential. Plate Q is $0\text{ V}$ and plate P is $-700\text{ V}$, so Q is higher.
Therefore the field at R points upward from Q towards P. This is option D.

A.explanation: Magnitude is 1000 times too small because $5.0\text{ mm}$ was not converted to metres, and direction is wrong as field points to the lower potential plate P.

B.explanation: Direction from Q at $0\text{ V}$ towards P at $-700\text{ V}$ is correct, but $1.4 \times 10^2\text{ N C}^{-1}$ uses $5.0$ mm as $5.0$ m.

C.explanation: Magnitude $1.4 \times 10^5\text{ N C}^{-1}$ is correct, but field cannot point from P at $-700\text{ V}$ towards Q at $0\text{ V}$ as that is from low to high potential.

D.explanation: Magnitude $700/0.0050 = 1.4 \times 10^5\text{ N C}^{-1}$ is correct and field points from higher potential Q towards lower potential P.
